Charles Schwab stock: October inflows set a record
sum: Charles Schwab stock drew renewed attention on Friday, November 13, after the company released its monthly activity report for October 2026. In a Business Wire press release carried by Yahoo Finance, Charles Schwab said core net new assets reached 66.5 billion US dollars, a record for an October.

The report listed total client assets of 13.27 trillion US dollars at the end of October. Schwab opened 409,000 new brokerage accounts during the month, marking the eighth consecutive month with at least 400,000 openings.

Client daily average trades totaled 10.6 million, with equities and exchange-traded funds driving engagement. Net ETF buying reached 37.0 billion US dollars, while mutual funds recorded net selling of 18.0 billion US dollars.

Client margin loan balances stood at 196.7 billion US dollars at month-end, which the company described as a record and 75 percent above year-end. Transactional sweep cash ended October at 485.8 billion US dollars after a 7.0 billion US dollar monthly decline.

For investors, the release provides a fresh view of client activity between quarterly earnings reports. Strong asset gathering, account formation and trading volumes support the scale of Schwab's brokerage and advisory operations, while the cash mix remains relevant to interest-sensitive revenue.

Stewart Cink shoots 63 to lead Charles Schwab Cup Championship
sum: Stewart Cink leads the Charles Schwab Cup Championship after the first round. At Phoenix Country Club, the defending champion opened with an 8-under 63 to sit one shot clear of the field heading into Friday. It is a strong start for a player with plenty at stake this week. Cink arrived in Arizona as the defending Charles Schwab Cup champion and at No. 1 in the season-long standings, 186,002 points ahead of rookie Zach Johnson.

The stakes are clear. Cink is chasing back-to-back Charles Schwab Cup titles, which no one has managed since Bernhard Langer won it from 2014 to 2016. He also returns to a tournament he won last year at 20-under 264. With three rounds still to play on a par-71 course measuring 6,860 yards, his 63 is only a first step. Still, nobody in the field went lower on Thursday.

The closest challenger is a World Golf Hall of Famer. Ernie Els shot a 7-under 64 and sits alone in second at 7 under, one stroke behind Cink. The South African has often played well at this event, and his round sets up a possible duel with the leader over the weekend.

Australia's Steve Allan is third on his own at 6 under after a 65. Allan, Els and Cink were level at 6 under at one point during the round. Cink then pulled ahead late, and Els finished one shot clear of Allan.
Three players share fourth at 5 under after rounds of 66: Jerry Kelly of the USA, Australia's Richard Green and Denmark's Søren Kjeldsen. All three trail by three shots.

Seven players are tied for seventh at 4 under after opening 67s. The group includes Germany's Alex Cejka, South Africa's Darren Fichardt, David Toms, Dicky Pride, Sweden's Freddie Jacobson, Argentina's Ricardo Gonzalez and Australia's Scott Hend. All of them are four shots off the lead.
Six more players are tied for 14th at 3 under after rounds of 68: Canada's Stephen Ames, Ben Crane, Rory Sabbatini, Timothy O'Neal, Tommy Gainey and Korea's Y.E. Yang.

sum: A trust linked to Charles R. Schwab, co-chairman of The Charles Schwab Corporation, sold 70,750 common shares on Monday, November 9, 2026, according to the reported SEC Form 4. The filing was signed on Tuesday, November 10, and also records a separate transfer of 31,850 shares as a bona fide gift.

The filing, reproduced by StockTitan, shows that the sale was executed in multiple trades at prices from 92.835 US dollars to 93.135 US dollars. The weighted-average sale price was 93.0074 US dollars per share, producing reported proceeds of 6.58 million US dollars.

The Form 4 lists both transactions as indirect holdings by a trust. After the reported transactions, the trust held 53,232,016 common shares. The filing also lists indirect holdings through a limited partnership, 188 Corp and Schwab's spouse as trustee.

The distinction between the two entries matters for investors. The November 9 transaction is an open-market sale, while the November 10 entry is a gift with no reported sale proceeds. The filing describes ownership changes but does not provide evidence of a shift in the company's business outlook, earnings expectations or capital allocation policy.
Charles Schwab stock traded at 83.61 euros on Lang & Schwarz at 12:39 CET on Thursday, November 12, 2026.

The disclosure adds a completed transaction to the recent sequence of ownership updates involving Charles R. Schwab. A single insider sale can reflect personal liquidity, estate planning or other considerations, so the filing alone does not establish a directional signal for the shares. Investors may instead watch whether further filings show repeated sales, changes in beneficial ownership or transactions by additional executives and directors.

sum: U.S. labor-market figures will set the main agenda for Charles Schwab investors next week. The October Employment Situation report is scheduled for Friday, November 6, at 8:30 a.m. Eastern Time, according to InvestingLive.

The calendar cited by the market publication calls for nonfarm payrolls to rise by 63,000, compared with 29,000 previously. The unemployment rate is expected to remain at 4.2%, while average hourly earnings are forecast to increase 0.3% month over month after 0.1% previously. The combination could influence expectations for interest rates and the trading environment for financial firms.

Charles Schwab entered the week with strong operating momentum. In its October 15 release, the company reported third-quarter net revenue of 7.171 billion U.S. dollars, up 17% from a year earlier. GAAP diluted earnings per share reached 1.62 U.S. dollars, while adjusted diluted earnings per share came to 1.69 U.S. dollars after 151 million U.S. dollars of pretax transaction-related costs.

Client activity also strengthened. Total client assets reached 13.33 trillion U.S. dollars at the end of September, and daily average trading volume increased 44% year over year to 10.7 million trades. Schwab said core net new assets totaled 190.4 billion U.S. dollars during the quarter.

For Schwab, the jobs report matters through both market activity and monetary policy expectations. A resilient labor market could support trading engagement, while wage pressure may keep attention on the interest-rate outlook. Softer hiring could raise growth concerns, even if it increases expectations for easier policy.

The Retail Trading Boom Is Back. Charles Schwab Is Quietly Cashing In.
sum: When investors look at the discount broker industry today, fresh new names like Robinhood (HOOD +3.21%) probably get more attention than established names like Charles Schwab (SCHW -1.18%). That likely makes sense, given that Charles Schwab is one of the oldest companies in the sector. However, it would be a mistake to dismiss this financial giant. Here's how Schwab is quietly benefiting from the retail trading boom that's underway.

In May 2026, Charles Schwab's customers held accounts worth $13.1 trillion dollars. That's a huge sum of money. For comparison's sake, Robinhood's total platform assets amounted to "only" $344 billion. That's not meant to be a put-down to Robinhood, which is a much younger company and has achieved impressive things in a very short period of time. It is meant to show just how large Charles Schwab's business really is. In fact, it was one of the companies that helped Space Exploration Technologies (SPCX +8.62%) go public.

It is easier to grow a small business, but that doesn't mean Charles Schwab isn't growing. The company's customer assets increased 27% year over year in May. That's a massive increase, helped along by rising stock prices and new accounts. According to the financial giant, "New brokerage accounts opened during the month totaled 461,000, an increase of 37% versus May 2025."

Every new account is a chance to earn more money from commissions, margin interest, and fee-generating services (from asset management services to the management fees earned from Schwab's own family of exchange-traded funds). On the trading front, the company hit a record daily average of 11.8 million trades in May. Margin loans, meanwhile, were up 38% from the end of 2025.

To be fair, Robinhood's growth opportunity is larger than Schwab's. But, as noted, it is easier to grow from a smaller base. There's a problem with that, as growth-enamored investors often push valuations to extreme levels. Notably, Robinhood's price-to-earnings ratio is 54x, while Schwab's is a far lower 19x.
Schwab is an industry giant that is quietly cashing in on the current trading boom. And you can buy it for less than half Robinhood's valuation.

After Earnings, Is Schwab Stock a Buy, a Sell, or Fairly Valued?
sum: Charles Schwab released its first-quarter earnings report on April 16. Here’s Morningstar’s take on Schwab’s earnings and stock.

Schwab reported strong quarterly results, generating 16% sales growth, 38% growth in adjusted EPS, and attracting an outstanding $140 billion in net new client assets. Still, shares traded down by a mid-single-digit percentage during April 16 trading on cash-sorting fears.

Why it matters: Schwab is the low-cost operator in the retail brokerage and registered investment advisor custody space, and we believe it will emerge as a long-term winner as a result, regardless of the ultimate vehicle of customer monetization. We’ve seen the firm reinvent its model twice already; first with asset management through its first-party funds and mutual fund marketplace, and second through Schwab Bank.

- Concerns seem to center on JPMorgan Chase’s planned launch of an artificial intelligence cash management tool, alluded to in Jamie Dimon’s annual letter to shareholders. The comments seem to portray that product as evolutionary rather than revolutionary, with Dimon suggesting that high-net-worth clients are already adept at cash sorting and that competition for customer deposits is already intense.

- We don’t expect Schwab to see material pressure here. The rates paid on sweep deposits are very low—just 0.19% during the quarter—but also comprise less than 4% of customer assets. Customers seem to accept that low cash sweep rates are the ticket to admission for an otherwise free, robust ecosystem of services that Schwab provides. If the bank’s cost of funding were to tick up, those services would invariably need to be monetized in other ways.
The bottom line: As we digest results, we’ve raised our fair value estimate to $114 from $111, due to quarterly outperformance and a more constructive expected short-term interest rate environment.

Key stats: The firm’s $5.6 billion in revenue and $1.43 in adjusted EPS edged our respective $5.5 billion and $1.27 estimates, driven by better-than-expected 15% growth in asset management and 20% growth in trading revenue.

sum: The Schwab U.S. Dividend Equity ETF (SCHD) was launched on October 20, 2011, and is a passively managed exchange traded fund designed to offer broad exposure to the Large Cap Value segment of the US equity market.

Companies that find themselves in the large cap category typically have a market capitalization above $10 billion. Overall, they are usually a stable option, with less risk and more sure-fire cash flows than mid and small cap companies.

While value stocks have lower than average price-to-earnings and price-to-book ratios, they also have lower than average sales and earnings growth rates. Looking at their long-term performance, value stocks have outperformed growth stocks in almost all markets. They are however likely to underperform growth stocks in strong bull markets.
Investors should also pay attention to an ETF's expense ratio. Lower cost products will produce better results than those with a higher cost, assuming all other metrics remain the same.
Annual operating expenses for this ETF are 0.06%, making it one of the least expensive products in the space.

Even though ETFs offer diversified exposure which minimizes single stock risk, it is still important to look into a fund's holdings before investing. Luckily, most ETFs are very transparent products that disclose their holdings on a daily basis.

However, retail investors can get exposure to all three companies today through the Ark Venture Fund (ARKVX +0.86%). Here are the important details.

SpaceX is an aerospace transportation company founded by Elon Musk in 2002. It designs, manufactures, and launches advanced rockets and spacecraft, and is particularly well known for its Starship system (the first fully reusable orbital rocket designed to return to the launch site) and Starlink satellite internet service.

SpaceX generated about $16 billion in revenue and about $8 billion in profit last year, according to Reuters. OpenAI is an artificial intelligence research company founded in 2015. Developers can also build OpenAI models into custom applications through Amazon Bedrock and Microsoft Foundry.

In February 2026, OpenAI's annual revenue run rate topped $25 billion, up 17% from $21.4 billion at the end of 2025, per The Information. The company currently makes most of its money from consumer products, primarily subscription fees from ChatGPT, but revenue from enterprise customers is projected to increase quickly in the years ahead as it releases new products and integrates advertising.

OpenAI closed its most recent funding round with a post-money valuation of $852 billion, which is 34 times its latest annualized sales figure. But that multiple should drop quickly. The fear isn't explicitly tied to the tax services these companies provide, but rather that cheap AI tools will soon be more widely available for a range of financial services offered by big companies, eating into margins.

It's a nearly identical fear that shook the software space last week. After Anthropic rolled out new tools for its Cowork agent aimed at professionals in the legal space, the entire sector sold off as investors eyed the potential for wider disruption.

Other brokerage stocks, such as Interactive Brokers and Morgan Stanley, fared slightly better on Tuesday. The fact that both firms cater to institutional traders implies that Wall Street is more concerned about retail-facing brokerage stocks.

items.t: Schwab discloses it's set to levy new $5-per-client, per-block-trade fees that could balloon cost for RIA custody clients by thousands of dollars
sum: The RIA custodian has posted the coming fee on its pricing schedule -- raising questions related to trade-away policies, best execution and payment-for-order-flow.
Charles Schwab & Co. is adding a new, flat $5-per-account fee for select RIA trades that could cost advisors tens of thousands of dollars annually to use more complex investing strategies.

The fee, effective Mar. 2, will be levied on block orders – a best execution* trading practice for pricing large trades that require “special handling" from its trading desk, and don't go through its payment-for-order-flow algorithms, according to the its latest price guide.

Only block-trades made through Schwab’s bread-and-butter algorithms** remain free. The charge will apply if orders need manual support from Schwab’s staff trading desk, or require ‘complex’ algorithms, specific market conditions, or quotation requests from third-party desks.

“Schwab isn't just recovering commission revenue, they're re-architecting their entire custody model around operational efficiency while creating stronger incentives for advisors to utilize their integrated trading infrastructure," says Greg O'Gara, strategic advisor at Datos Insights.

“The $5 [per] account, block trading fee is one piece of a larger strategy to channel order flow through highly automated channels where operational costs are lowest and revenue capture, via payment-for-order-flow, is highest,” he adds, in an email.
The block-trade fee is “a strategic re-pricing of trading complexity," says Tim Welsh, a former Schwab director and now president of Larkspur, Calif., consultancy Nexus Strategy, in an email.
